newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP sees rise in Magma copper reserves.
newsitem.headline: BHP sees rise in Magma copper reserves.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd managing director John Prescott said on Friday that he expected there would be a rise in measured copper reserves at the company's Magma operations in the United states.
"There will be a build up in the reserves," Prescott told a news conference held after the release of 1996/97 (June/May) profit results.

Prescott said there were some positives in the Magma operation that had yet to be reflected in BHP's accounts, referring to the expected increase in reserves. He did not quantify the expected increase.
The company said earlier on Friday that net profit in the year to May 31 fell by 60.8 percent to A$410 million after abnormal items of nearly A$1 billion.
More than half of the abnormal loss, A$550 million, was due to write-downs at the North American copper operations.
BHP is the world's second largest copper producer, trailing the state-owned Codelco group in Chile.
It acquired Magma for US$2.4 billion in January 1996 and is the largest shareholder in the Escondida copper mine in Chile.
